title: disposition
description: An EXTERNAL verdict on a filed finding. The only ground truth this harness has. Everything else in the repo is the harness grading itself. One record per (report, adjudicating party). Append-only.

finding_ref.description: the finding id or package path this disposition adjudicates

report_id.description: the external report identifier: H1 report number, GHSA id, issue url. Empty when the program does not issue one.

program.description: the adjudicating program, e.g. 'HackerOne/Netflix', 'GitHub Security Advisories/Klever', 'Google OSS VRP'

recorded_at.description: when this record was written (not when the vendor decided)

decided_at.description: when the external party decided, if known

our_severity.description: the band THIS HARNESS assigned before filing. Never back-edit it to match the vendor — that destroys the measurement.

our_vector.description: CVSS vector we filed, if any

their_severity.description: the band the external party assigned. `not-assigned` when they accepted or rejected without grading — common for Informative closures.

outcome.description: What the external party DID. Kept separate from severity because the two dissociate: Klever closed our report not-accepted while publishing their own advisory crediting us as reporter. A schema that forces those into one field forces a lie.

bounty_usd.description: amount paid, if any. 0 is meaningful; absent means unknown.

source.description: How we know. A disposition with no retrievable source is hearsay, and hearsay is what this ledger exists to replace.

ref.description: file:line for repo_record, a URL for external_url/vendor_advisory

confidence.description: How firmly this record is established. `operator_recall` is legitimate and common, and MUST be marked so that a calibration run can report how much of its basis is unverified.

notes.description: Anything that would change how a later reader weighs this record. Disagreements, partial credit, a finder credited alongside us.

their_rating.description: The external party's rating VERBATIM, in their own vocabulary. Google Bug Hunters uses priority/severity (`P2`, `S4`); HackerOne uses its own bands; Immunefi uses named impacts. `their_severity` maps those onto a common ladder so deltas are computable, and mapping loses information. This field keeps the original so a later reader can re-map it or challenge the mapping. Record it whenever the program does not speak in CVSS bands.

novelty.description: Whether the finding was NEW to the program. A duplicate is external confirmation the bug is REAL — it is a novelty failure, not a validity failure, and Google states plainly that duplicates earn no reward or credit. Keeping this separate from `outcome` is what lets the ledger answer two different questions: duplicates validate our DETECTION, and only non-duplicates test our SEVERITY calibration. Folding them together would destroy both signals.
